name: command-palette
description: Cmd+K style modal command interface with search and keyboard navigation

changes.note: Nested components keep their own parts. The stylesheet reached the overlay, panel, search, list, groups and items with descendant selectors, so a component nested inside with parts of the same name took this one's styles. Parts are root > overlay and panel; panel > search-wrapper > search, or panel > search when there is no wrapper; panel > list > group > group-label and item, or list > item when there are no groups; item > item-label and kbd; and empty in the list or the panel. Every part rule is now a child chain from the root, with the hops in :where(), so no rule changes specificity. No change for markup that follows the template.

The kbd part sets font-variant-ligatures: var(--mono-ligatures, none). --mono-ligatures is a new typography token that defaults to none; Cascadia Code and JetBrains Mono, both named by --font-mono, ligate by default, so a shortcut hint such as -> was drawn as one joined glyph. Set --mono-ligatures: normal to get a face's ligatures back.

Cmd/Ctrl+K is matched case-insensitively and has one owner. The shortcut compared e.key to "k", so Caps Lock ("K") missed it; it now lowercases the key and falls back to the physical KeyK on a non-Latin layout, and ignores Alt, Shift (Cmd+Shift+K is a browser and app chord of its own), auto-repeat and IME composition. Every instance listened on document with no opt-out, so a page with three palettes opened three stacked focus traps: the handler now stands down on an event something else already prevented, so the first palette in listener order (or an app handler that pre-empts it) owns the press, and a palette whose root has left the document without destroy() no longer claims it. New boolean prop data-no-shortcut opts an instance out entirely; it is read on each press, so it can be toggled at runtime.

Closing no longer sends focus to an opener that has gone or is hidden. The palette restored focus to whatever was focused when it opened, even an element that had since left the document or sat inside another overlay that had closed underneath it (a palette opened from inside a dialog, say). Focus now returns only to an opener that is still in the document and not under [hidden], and only if focus is still in the palette or on body when it closes.

data-highlighted and data-hidden are now declared. The controller has always written both onto the options (active descendant and filtered-out respectively) and the CSS has always styled them, but no manifest named them. They are states rather than props because a controller writes them: a state is the runtime's vocabulary, a prop is what an author types. 0.8-10's undeclared-attribute rule now makes this class of drift impossible: an attribute a component's CSS selects on that its manifest never declares fails the registry gate.

search.description: Search input with role=combobox for filtering commands. Sits in the search-wrapper, or directly in the panel when there is none

group.description: Group container with label and items

item.description: Individual command item with role=option. A child of a group, or of the list when there are no groups

empty.description: Empty state shown when no commands match. Inside the list, or directly in the panel

kbd.description: Keyboard shortcut hint displayed in items

search-wrapper.description: Row holding the search input and its leading icon

group-label.description: Heading naming a group of commands

item-label.description: The command text inside an item, beside its icon and kbd hint

highlighted.description: The active descendant of the command list — the item arrow keys have moved to, mirrored in aria-activedescendant. The controller writes it; only one item carries it at a time

hidden.description: An item filtered out by the search query — and, on a group, a group whose every item is filtered out. The controller writes both; hidden items are skipped by keyboard navigation and by the empty-state check

noShortcut.description: This palette does not listen for Cmd/Ctrl+K; open it from code with open(). Use it on every palette but one when a page has several. Read on each key press

required_attrs: aria-activedescendant on the combobox, naming the active option while the list is open

keyboard.Cmd+K / Ctrl+K: toggle command palette (case-insensitive; not with Shift or Alt; off under data-no-shortcut)

a11y.notes: A search field kept in the page joins the page's undo history, so Cmd/Ctrl+Z after closing the palette can undo the search text instead of the user's last edit. Render the palette with l-if if that matters.
